quest.title: Festival Utsava
quest.description: You returned to Vanarana with Arama after parting with Arana and Rana. It's finally time for Festival Utsava.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back, Araja!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Finally! Everyone's been waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Festival Utsava has started, but it's not in full swing yet since Nara friends didn't get back till now.

choices.text: There are so many Aranara here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's been a real grind adventuring like this huh. Let's just enjoy the festivities right now, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Yes, you must enjoy yourselves, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Yes. I'll see you later.

choices.text: Can we prepare the Bija once the festival is over?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: As far as I know, yes.

talks.objective: Enjoy Festival Utsava with Aranara in the Vanarana in the dream

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The Aranara disperse following the duet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that was great! Your playing and the Aranara song were both awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: #Yeah, Nara {NICKNAME} is awesome! I'd love to travel with you and remember your songs!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: #Such a radiant melody. How exciting! Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, and your song... What an epic tale!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not calling me "Golden Nara" anymore?

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: I'm short on experience, but if the stories were true, the glow from Nara Varuna's song might have been dimmer than yours!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: #Aradasa is right. Please take these as tokens of our appreciation, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, this is a lot of flowers...

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: "Even though the horizon is so gray, it's such a blessing to meet you..."

response.speaker: Aradasa
response.text: "...Singing your song forever is the pact between you and me."

choices.text: Thank you. I'll cherish your gift.

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon guesses that Festival Utsava is coming to an end...

choices.text: And we're one step closer to getting the Bija.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should ask Araja what to do next... Hey, where did Araja and Arama go?

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: Oh, they went that way after the duet.

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: #I do want to tell Nara {NICKNAME} that...

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: #Arasudraka has learned why Nara {NICKNAME} entered Vanarana. Your and Arana's friend will be fine.

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: Also, no matter how dark the sky and land get, as long as your spirit emits warmth like a golden sun, there will always be hope.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't worry, Arasudraka! {NICKNAME} has always been like that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll get going now. Farewell!

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: Farewell!

choices.text: Finally, light at the end of the tunnel.
It's a good thing that no Whopperflowers showed up.

dialogues.speaker: Aranishat
dialogues.text: Aralila, Nara have a incantation to find Nara in hiding. It goes like this: "Curry, curry in the air~ Hungry children it's time to come home~♪"

dialogues.speaker: Aralila
dialogues.text: But what's curry?

dialogues.speaker: Aranishat
dialogues.text: Oh, I don't know. But I heard little Nara will come when they hear this incantation! So, you can try it if you're looking for little Nara!

dialogues.speaker: Araesha
dialogues.text: Festival Utsava will have Araesha's tasty riddles, which are also sweet and fragrant! I heard that Nara like sweet and fragrant things...

dialogues.speaker: Araesha
dialogues.text: So you'll love this sweet and fragrant Festival Utsava, right, Nara?

dialogues.speaker: Arakanta
dialogues.text: Thank you, Nara! Arakanta is so happy!

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: #Oh? It's Nara {NICKNAME}! We learned many lost tunes thanks to you, Paimon, and Arama.

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: You're well acquainted with the art of singing, right?

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: Then please... What was the Nara phrase again? "Let me borrow your ears"... or something like that.

choices.text: I think you meant "lend me your ears."

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: Is that how it's supposed to be? Eh, anyway, let's meet again later!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: #Hahaha, Nara {NICKNAME}'s really funny.

dialogues.speaker: Arayasa
dialogues.text: #"Even if you cover {M#her}{F#his} eyes in gloom, you can't take away the light from {M#her}{F#his} heart..."

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: #You're back, Nara {NICKNAME}! A Festival Utsava with you is a tale fit for songs!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Oh my, I'm so touched...

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: Golden Nara, we shall sing together! Please take the lead!

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: May this song echo in Vanarana forever!

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Nara's "taste of happiness" is so strange... But since Nara is happy, Arapacati and her brothers shall be happy too!

dialogues.speaker: Arasaka
dialogues.text: The "taste of happiness" is good, of course. B—But it's not just about the sugar.

dialogues.speaker: Arachatora
dialogues.text: The Head Mushroom helped too! The Head Mushroom I've always dreamed about! Its aroma... Ahh!

dialogues.speaker: Araphala
dialogues.text: And don't... don't forget about the Unrivaled Fresh Fruit...

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: Water from Vanarana too! Soup with "the taste of happiness" can only be made with the best water!

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: Hey, it's the Golden Nara! Perfect timing!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: Gold is a wonderful color, the same as sunshine. That's what I'd like to call you on this important occasion!

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: #Regardless, your name shall be recorded in our songs. Nara {NICKNAME} is a good name, very lyrical!

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: #"The {M#boy}{F#girl} whose eyes and soul are as golden as the sun, thy name is Nara {NICKNAME}."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what about Paimon? Don't forget Paimon now!

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: "The pearl in moonlight, pure as silver, thy name is Paimon..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, Paimon wants to hear more! Maybe something that lauds our friendship too...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}! Paimon!

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: You're here! Everybody's having a great time at the festival.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's always nice to have someone to help out and play with, right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #No, not in that way! We're happy because we made friends with Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Although Aranakin, Aranaga, and Aragaru don't remember you, the forest does. The story will live on.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Yeah, the singing of a Nara friend with Aranara is the most important part of the festival in the story! Song gatherers, are you ready?

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: "From the first cry after birth, this is the moment you've been preparing for..."

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: Stupid Arayasa, only baby Nara are born and would cry.

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: We're ready! And so is the ancient "stage" where it will take place!

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: It was Aramuhukunda before me, and there will be other song gatherers after me to make it grow. It's been waiting for a long time to hear the duet between Nara and Aranara again.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #I'm very much looking forward to it as well. Are you ready, Nara {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #According to how it was done before, you should be playing instruments too, right? Paimon can't wait for your performance, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Don't worry, just use the instrument you're used to and play it at your own pace.

response.speaker: Arakavi
response.text: Well then, Golden Nara, we shall sing together! Please take the lead!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Go, Nara {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Huh. Even someone as mighty as Nara {NICKNAME} can get nervous?

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: "Gold and silver, the colors of the sun and moon, are the reflection of their friendship."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not bad! Adding a few lines praising Paimon's wisdom would be nice, too!

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: "The paths of stars, of flowing water, are all an open aranyaka to the silver one. The riddle is the moonlight's bait, the wisdom is the pearl's glimmer."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Very poetic! Y'know, Paimon's also very brave... sooo, get Paimon's drift?

response.speaker: Arayasa
response.text: "Swelling like a specter, surging ahead like a boar..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, who are you calling a Specter? What a letdown!

talks.objective: Play a melody by the stage

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Actually, I've been wanting to ask you something. Why do Nara sleep?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I see! Aranara "hibernate" only when a great, great danger is present. We turn into tiny seeds and go into dreamless slumbers.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But we will be isolated from others, and that's rather scary. Not to mention having to accumulate a lot of memories to change back into our previous forms...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But you Nara are different. You must sleep often, and that's the only way you can dream. Dreams are precious, so I understand... But it is strange. You have had very few dreams lately, big Nara...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Regardless, you can sleep here without worries. We will guard your dreams and stop bad things like Vanagni from getting in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds good, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gah, you and your mentions of dreams... Paimon almost feels like meeting you and spending the festival with you might just all be a dream Paimon had after eating those mushrooms, and that all this will vanish once Paimon wakes up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will we still see you when we wake up?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Of course!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good night!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Farewell!

choices.text: I don't know. I think sleeping is a waste of time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh? Don't you think sleep is pretty comfortable, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Aragaru
dialogues.text: Hehe, Festival Utsava, so lively! Vanarana is filled with joy!

dialogues.speaker: Aranakin
dialogues.text: But Festival Utsava will end. Nara friends of Aranara might leave too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The forest will remember.

dialogues.speaker: Aranaga
dialogues.text: The forest will remember, but...

dialogues.speaker: Aragaru
dialogues.text: I pray that no wind shall blow away our happiness; that there shall be rain to wet the earth and keep our Nara friends a while longer...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Oh my, I am so happy! I hope you will be happy too. Our greatest wish during Festival Utsava is to see our Nara friends happy.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Nara time is much more precious than Aranara time, so I will not keep you from enjoying yourselves. Go look for Arakavi later. He is also preparing for the Festival Utsava ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: The last Festival Utsava took place during Nara Varuna's time! In many tales and recollections, Marana was everywhere back then.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Trees died, and lush plains turned brown. It rained filthy red water... Red, not the lovely apple red. Very horrifying!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: I'm glad I don't remember it now. Many children returned to Sarva before they were done growing into Vasara Trees. But there were still Nara Varuna and Festival Utsava.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yes. At the time, you must have been a young Aranara sapling like me!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Right. I have lost a lot of memories, but still can recall Nara's tears. Salty drops fell from {M#her}{F#his} eyes, but I wasn't afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #{M#She}{F#He} spoke to me at length about our adventures in the forest, and thus the tales were preserved. Then, {M#she}{F#he} left.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #I wonder where {M#she}{F#he} is now? {M#She}{F#He} was very much like you, Nara {NICKNAME}. You two might be Nara, but you are shining like the warm, golden sun.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Drifting seeds are destined to flourish on nice soil... same for Nara! One day, the wind in Nara's hearts will stop, halting their steps.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #But Nara {NICKNAME} is not like ordinary Nara. Nara {NICKNAME} will keep traveling, and will perhaps run into Nara Varuna someday!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Yes, but you forgot, Arama, that Nara are not Aranara. Their time is short.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Nara Varuna couldn't live as long as trees, nor share dreams and memories as we do. How lonely and lamentable the Nara are.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #...Right. If only Nara {NICKNAME} were an Aranara! If so, we would've known each other from way before and shared so many memories.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: The forest will remember. I'll bring all of Vanarana's memories to meet Aramuhukunda in Sarva, like rivers converging into the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: A very long time ago, Vanarana was destroyed in that Nara catastrophe. Since then, Aranara made dreams their home and distanced themselves from Nara.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Only Nara Varuna has always been friends with Aranara and continued helping everyone after the destruction. Only then did Aranara trust Nara again, little by little.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #When we parted, {M#she}{F#he} told me that, maybe one day, another Golden Nara would come to us, and {M#he}{F#she} would bring us even better memories.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #I think that with you and Nara {NICKNAME}, perhaps it's time for us to walk, sing, and play with Nara in the forests once again.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #But everybody trusts Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon because they're genuinely good. It wouldn't be a problem if all Nara are nice like Nara {NICKNAME} and Nara Varuna!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: You sound like an old Nara, Araja!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm very happy to have the festival and give the flowers to the Golden Nara, but I'm also reminded of a lot of other things...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arama, Araja! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't tell Paimon you ran away because you didn't like how {NICKNAME} played?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #No! Nara {NICKNAME}'s performance was a bright ray of sunshine. It felt very, very good.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #But the Bija is crucial to Arana's and Nara {NICKNAME}'s wish, so I had to get ready.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, the Bija...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I went looking for the Fane of Ashvattha right after the song ended.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds like it had something to do with the concourses we visited before.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Paimon is as bright as moonlight. That's where Ashvattha's Tree of Dreams is. It's an ancient, sturdy Vasara Tree that's able to produce Bija.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: However, I don't remember the location, nor am I able to leave Vanarana's dream, so it's all up to Arama to find it.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Worry not. Like Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon would say, "I got this!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's confused. You said that you can't leave, Araja. Can't you go to places in a jiffy like Arama?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: I've been limited to moving only in Vanarana's dreams since a long, long time ago.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: A "Tree of Dreams" is required to anchor a dream this big, and I became that tree so everyone would have a home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How can this be...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: What's the matter, Paimon? It's a good thing for me to house so many big dreams and be with everyone.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yeah, I want to be a great Aranara like Araja when I grow up, hosting many dreams like a tree with many leaves!

choices.text: Aranara have a different way of thinking...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon gets it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that eccentric Aranara we met before also said that Bija is yielded from the extraction of memories and dreams.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that true? Can Aranara lose their memory?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: That's probably the case... but I can no longer recall it now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what should we do now?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #You got a lot of flowers during the festival, right, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not just during the festival! We got some from Aranakin, Aragaru, and Aranaga too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wishes they could remember all the adventures we had together...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Don't worry, no memories will be lost! The forest will remember, just like the rivers emptying into the sea, before being turned into the rain splashing down unto the earth.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Give me all the flowers, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They're mementos of Aranara's friendship and are precious to us. What do you need them for, Arama?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I'm putting my flowers and theirs together!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since you put it that way, Arama...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You hand Arama all of the flowers.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Arama weaves a garland out of the flowers, including its own, and puts it on your head.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #Oh, it's so pretty. It looks great on you, Nara {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: This garland represents the blessings that we Aranara, as well as all of Vanarana, want to bestow upon our favorite Nara.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Unlike you Nara, we Aranara can communicate in our dreams.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Any sadness can be shared among all Aranara to soften its blow, and we share our joys as well.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #When Nara {NICKNAME} wears the garland, we'll be able to share the load on your mind, and we can protect you when you have nightmares.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #I should be thanking you, Nara {NICKNAME}, for accepting our flowers! That gives us greater joy than soaking in the sun, drinking sweet water, and dreaming nice things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants a garland too!

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: I doubt that's necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why not?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} will be facing many great dangers and experiencing great sadness. We can ward off some of {M#his}{F#her} nightmares through the garland.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #On the other hand, Nara {NICKNAME} will protect Paimon from nightmares. You will always be together and will share both joy and sorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We're the best of friends, after all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what should we do now?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: We're going to offer the Vasoma Fruit at the Fane of Ashvattha. Then we can produce the Bija with Arana!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I have studied you Nara before. Unlike Aranara, you have to "sleep" when the moon is up, and you come out only after the sun has risen.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Would you like to sleep, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it, Paimon's pretty bushed from all the fun today.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: You can rest in my house, if you'd like. Vanarana will guard your dreams.

choices.text: I'll take the offer. I'm feeling rather tired.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}, for accepting our flowers! That gives us greater joy than soaking in the sun, drinking sweet water, and dreaming nice things.

choices.text: We met an odd Aranara once...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes. It said that Bija is yielded from the extraction of memories and dreams.

choices.text: Araja, what do you mean you "can't leave"...?
I totally didn't forget that, ahaha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon blames it on Festival Utsava feast that {NICKNAME} made. It was so delicious that Paimon got distracted.

talks.objective: Head to Araja's house to rest
Head to Araja's house to rest

dialogues.speaker: Aranakula
dialogues.text: #This feels just like the time Nara Varuna celebrated Festival Utsava with Aranara all over again... Aranakula hasn't been so happy in a very long time, Nara {NICKNAME}. *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Arakara
dialogues.text: Viparyas hate tears. Festival Utsava is a happy festival. Aranakula will play a happy song for Viparyas!

dialogues.speaker: Arayasa
dialogues.text: "This is our song..."

dialogues.speaker: Arapandu
dialogues.text: The last time we had such a lively Festival Utsava was when Nara Varuna came to Vanarana...

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: The festival may be fun, but nothing lasts forever.

dialogues.speaker: Arakunti
dialogues.text: Just like how Nilotpala Lotuses in the water never stay in bloom. They must always close sometime.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, for coming to Vanarana and celebrating Festival Utsava with us Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan wants to spend more time together with you, good friends...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes! You will be fine, Nara {NICKNAME}! Hearing your song gives us courage to even face Marana!

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: *sigh* This is great...

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: As long as your heart emits golden and warm lights like the sun, there will always be hope!

dialogues.speaker: Arayasa
dialogues.text: "...Singing your song forever is the pact between you and me."

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: You go get some rest. I want to stay and reminisce a little.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Later, Ararycan will return to the bad dirty stuff, and see if anything bad happens.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: #Ararycan is a good friend to Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, forever!

dialogues.speaker: Aragaru
dialogues.text: Aranakin, Aranaga, my heart feels empty. Have I forgotten something?

dialogues.speaker: Aranakin
dialogues.text: Aragaru is "hungry" just like Nara?

dialogues.speaker: Aranaga
dialogues.text: What is it... Can't remember...

dialogues.speaker: Aranakula
dialogues.text: #This feels just like the time Nara Varuna celebrated Festival Utsava with Aranara all over again... Aranakula hasn't been so happy in a very long time, Nara {NICKNAME}. *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Arakara
dialogues.text: Viparyas hate tears. Festival Utsava is a happy festival. Aranakula will play a happy song for Viparyas!
